(in pm) out of the options given below
solution:
Vanderwaal's radius is considered in case of neon, which
normally has a large value. Also, in neon, the valence shell is
completely filled with electrons. As a result, there are interelectronic
repulsions and thus electron cloud expands. So, atomic radii of neon is
greater than that of fluorine.

1M solution with a strong base is -55.95 kJ/mol. If acid HA requires
1.4 complete ionization and enthalpy of
neutralization of the strong monobasic acid with a strong monoacidic
base is -57.3 kJ/mol. What is the ionization of the weak acid in
molar solution ?
solution:
$HA - H^{+} + A^{-};\Delta_{r}H = 1.4kJ/mol$
$\Delta H_{neutalization\ } = \Delta H_{ionization\ } + \Delta_{r}H\ of\ \left( H^{+} + {OH}^{-} \rightarrow H_{2}O \right)$
$- 55.95 = \Delta H_{ionization\ } - 57.3$
$\Delta H_{ionization\ }\ for\ 1MHA = 1.35kJ/mol$ heat utilized by 1 M acid for ionization
$= \frac{1.35}{1.4} \times 100 = 96.43\%$
So, acid is$\ 100 - 96.43 = 3.57\%$ ionized.
